question: Does a conservative distribution of return-path lengths, represented by one universal baryon-size-scaled diffusion kernel, improve apparent lensing morphology across ten clusters and transfer to three cluster holdouts?

formula.endpoint: D=exp[(ell^2/2)*laplacian] B = G_ell convolved with B
formula.universal_length: ell=q*R80_b, with one dimensionless q for every cluster
formula.conservation: B_20 and D are separately positive and unit normalized inside 250 kpc
formula.backtracking: P(origin i|destination d) proportional to w_i*exp[-|d-x_i|^2/(2*ell^2)]

data.spent_disclosure: The clusters and split are globally spent by P0568/P0572; P0592 is prospective only to the diffusion formula.

selection: Choose q and f by equal-cluster mean Lenstool-ensemble JSD on seven development systems; transfer unchanged to three holdout systems, all 100 Lenstool realizations, and GLAFIC controls.
claim_limits: The ten-cluster baryon proxy is member F160W light and omits hot gas, ICL, and stellar mass-to-light variation; MACS J0416 showed that gas can dominate the source field.
The target maps are standard-GR convergence reconstructions and reuse observations across methods.
Diffusion is an endpoint propagator, not yet a covariant causal field theory; it does not specify propagation time, signal speed, or the hidden coordinate.
A Gaussian endpoint can describe many mechanisms besides curved gravity paths, so transfer is necessary but not sufficient evidence.
